stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and has 12 AWS accounts. Employees sign in to business applications through the company's external SAML 2.0 identity provider. The company also runs a mobile app for its customers. The engineers must sign in once and use the AWS CLI with short-term credentials in every account. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: The engineers must sign in once

options.text: Use IAM Identity Center with the external identity provider as the identity source, and assign permission sets that give access to the AWS accounts.
options.why: IAM Identity Center [configures all the necessary user permissions](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-configures-account-permissions-automatically) in the assigned accounts, and its users get temporary credentials at each sign-in.

options.text: Use an Amazon Cognito user pool that federates with the identity providers that the users already have, and an identity pool that issues temporary AWS credentials.
options.why: Amazon Cognito is [not a supported identity source](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-cognito-is-not-an-identity-source) of IAM Identity Center, and it serves customer-facing applications, not the workforce.

options.text: Create an IAM user with MFA and an access key for each person in each AWS account, and rotate every access key on a fixed monthly schedule.
options.why: [IAM users are granted long-term credentials](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials), and the stem asks for short-term credentials, so rotation does not fix the problem.

options.text: Create an IAM identity provider and IAM roles in every AWS account, and build a custom broker that exchanges each sign-in for temporary role credentials.
options.why: It works, but [direct federation to each AWS account](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-wa-two-federation-approaches) repeats the provider and the roles in every account and adds a broker to build.

explanation: The engineers are the company's workforce, and they need many accounts. With an external provider [you only federate once](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-one-point-of-federation), and IAM Identity Center [creates and manages IAM roles](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users) for each permission set in each assigned account. In the AWS CLI version 2, [the CLI manages short-term credentials automatically](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-cli-v2-sign-in-short-term-credentials).
takeaway: Employees who need many AWS accounts get IAM Identity Center with permission sets, not Amazon Cognito.
twin: If the stem said "The app's customers must sign in with Google and upload photos to Amazon S3 with short-term credentials" instead: Amazon Cognito, because an identity pool issues [temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool).
say: Employees in many accounts means IAM Identity Center with permission sets.

stem: A company has a mobile app in which customers record home-repair requests. Customers already sign in to the app through an Amazon Cognito user pool, and the app sends the user pool tokens to the company's API. A new feature saves photos from the device directly to an Amazon S3 bucket with temporary credentials, and each customer's photos go under a prefix for that customer. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?
keywords: directly to an Amazon S3 bucket with temporary credentials

options.text: Send the user pool ID token with each Amazon S3 request, and add a bucket policy that allows requests that carry a valid token from the pool.
options.why: The user pool is there to [issue JSON web tokens (JWTs)](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool) for the app, and Amazon S3 needs AWS credentials, which an identity pool gives.

options.text: Create one IAM user for the app, keep its access key in encrypted storage on each device, and allow the user to write to the bucket.
options.why: The IAM guide says not to embed access keys with the app, [even in encrypted storage](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-mobile-app-never-embed-access-keys), and an access key is not temporary.

options.text: Add a Cognito identity pool with the user pool as its provider, and give the authenticated role access to the prefix that matches each identity ID.
options.why: The identity pool accepts the user pool token, and a role policy that uses the identity ID gives each customer [access to their own folder](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-identity-id-per-user-s3-folder).

options.text: Add a Cognito identity pool with the user pool as its provider, and give the authenticated role write access to every prefix in the bucket.
options.why: It works, but every signed-in customer could write into the prefixes of all other customers, which is less secure than a role that uses the identity ID.
options.misconception: treats temporary credentials as safe even when the role reaches the data of every customer

explanation: A user pool signs customers in, and an identity pool exchanges the token for [temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool). Each user gets an identity ID, and a policy that uses it gives each user [access to their own folder](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-identity-id-per-user-s3-folder). No AWS key ships with the app.
takeaway: App users reach Amazon S3 through an identity pool, with a role scoped to each identity ID.
twin: If the stem said "the app calls the company's API and nothing else" instead: the user pool tokens are enough, because API Gateway accepts a call when [the supplied token is valid](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-cognito-user-pools-authorizer).
say: Add an identity pool, and scope the role to each user's identity ID.

stem: A company has an Active Directory domain in its on-premises data center and a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the data center and a VPC. The company is moving several workloads to AWS. The domain controllers can be reached from the VPC. Employees must sign in to Amazon WorkSpaces with their existing AD credentials, and user accounts must remain only in the on-premises directory. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: user accounts must remain only in the on-premises directory

options.text: Create a Simple AD directory in the VPC, and create a two-way trust between the Simple AD directory and the on-premises domain.
options.why: Simple AD [does not support multi-factor authentication (MFA), trust relationships](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-simple-ad-unsupported-features), so it cannot trust the on-premises domain.

options.text: Create an AD Connector in the VPC that points to the on-premises domain controllers, and register the directory with the AWS services that need it.
options.why: AD Connector [forwards sign-in requests to your on-premises Active Directory](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-ad-connector-is-a-proxy), so WorkSpaces uses the existing accounts and no copy of the directory exists in AWS.

options.text: Launch Amazon EC2 instances in the VPC as additional domain controllers of the on-premises domain, and let Active Directory replicate the whole domain to the instances.
options.why: Replicated domain controllers on EC2 hold a copy of every user account, which breaks the requirement that the accounts stay in the on-premises directory.
options.misconception: believes that a replica domain controller in AWS keeps the user accounts on premises

options.text: Create an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory in the VPC, and create a two-way forest trust between that directory and the on-premises domain.
options.why: It works, but it adds [a highly available pair of domain controllers](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-managed-ad-dc-pair-across-azs) and a second domain to operate, and no workload here needs a domain in AWS.

explanation: WorkSpaces needs the employees' AD sign-in, and the accounts stay on premises. [AD Connector is a proxy service](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-ad-connector-is-a-proxy), and Directory Service [does not replicate any of your directory data](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-ad-connector-no-data-replicated). It needs a virtual private network [(VPN) connection or Direct Connect](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-ad-connector-needs-vpn-or-direct-connect), and the stem gives the VPN.
takeaway: Users who stay in the on-premises directory and sign in to AWS applications point to AD Connector.
twin: If the stem said "Amazon RDS for SQL Server databases must use Windows Authentication with the employees' existing AD accounts" instead: AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a trust, because RDS is [compatible with AWS Managed Microsoft AD only](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-rds-needs-managed-ad).
say: AD Connector forwards each sign-in to the on-premises domain controllers and keeps no copy.

stem: A company uses IAM Identity Center for access to 30 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The identity source is an on-premises Active Directory that is connected through AD Connector. The company is moving all workforce identities to Okta. Employees must sign in to the AWS accounts with their Okta credentials, and the company wants to automate the creation of new hires in IAM Identity Center. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)
keywords: moving all workforce identities to Okta
automate the creation of new hires

options.text: Keep AD Connector as the identity source, and add Okta to IAM Identity Center as a second identity source for the employees who use Okta.
options.why: IAM Identity Center connects [only one directory or one SAML 2.0 identity provider](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-one-identity-source-at-a-time) at a time.

options.text: Change the identity source of IAM Identity Center to an external identity provider, and connect Okta through SAML 2.0 with the IAM Identity Center metadata.
options.why: Okta replaces Active Directory, and with an external provider IAM Identity Center keeps [no authentication material](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-external-idp-no-passwords-stored), so Okta checks each sign-in.

options.text: Create an IAM SAML identity provider for Okta in each of the 30 member accounts, and create IAM roles in each account that trust the provider.
options.why: It works for sign-in, but [direct federation to each AWS account](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-wa-two-federation-approaches) repeats the provider and the roles in every member account.

options.text: Connect Okta to an Amazon Cognito user pool, and set the user pool as the identity source of IAM Identity Center for all employees.
options.why: Amazon Cognito is [not a supported identity source](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-cognito-is-not-an-identity-source) of IAM Identity Center.

options.text: Turn on automatic provisioning in IAM Identity Center, and configure Okta to send users and groups to the SCIM endpoint with a bearer token.
options.why: SCIM gives [automatic provisioning (synchronization) of user and group information](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-scim-automatic-provisioning), so new hires appear without manual work.

explanation: Okta becomes the one identity source: SAML 2.0 signs employees in, and SCIM creates and updates users and groups. Identities [must be provisioned into IAM Identity Center](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-provision-before-assign) before you assign permission sets, and SCIM does that work. Plan the switch, because a new source [might remove all user and group assignments](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-change-source-may-remove-assignments).
takeaway: An external identity provider uses SAML 2.0 for sign-in and SCIM to create users in IAM Identity Center.
twin: If the stem said "new hires are added by hand" instead: SAML 2.0 is enough for sign-in, but each user [must be provisioned into IAM Identity Center](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-provision-before-assign) before an assignment.

stem: A company runs a web application whose users sign in through an Amazon Cognito user pool. The application calls a REST API in Amazon API Gateway, and AWS Lambda functions run behind the API. The company must restrict the API so that it accepts requests only from users who signed in to the application. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
keywords: accepts requests only from users who signed in

options.text: Set the API methods to AWS_IAM authorization, create an IAM user with an access key for each customer, and sign each request to the API with that access key.
options.why: [IAM users are granted long-term credentials](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials), and a key for every customer adds key management and request signing to the application.

options.text: Create a Lambda authorizer that downloads the signing keys of the user pool, validates each token in custom code, and returns an IAM policy.
options.why: It works, but the team writes and maintains token checks, although you can [let Amazon API Gateway validate the token](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-validates-user-pool-token) of the user pool.

options.text: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the API stage, and allow requests only from the IP address ranges of the users of the application.
options.why: An IP address does not show who signed in, and the users connect from changing networks, so the rule does not check the sign-in.
options.misconception: believes that a firewall rule can tell whether a user signed in to the application

options.text: Create an authorizer of the COGNITO_USER_POOLS type for the user pool, enable it on the API methods, and send the user's token in the Authorization header.
options.why: The client sends its user pool token, and API Gateway lets the call through when [the supplied token is valid](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-cognito-user-pools-authorizer), with no code to write.

explanation: API Gateway can check user pool tokens itself: you can [let Amazon API Gateway validate the token](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-validates-user-pool-token) and gate access to the API. The client signs in, sends its token, and the call succeeds when [the supplied token is valid](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-cognito-user-pools-authorizer). The Lambda functions receive requests from signed-in users, and the team writes no token code.
takeaway: An API Gateway REST API accepts Cognito user pool tokens through a user pool authorizer, without custom code.
twin: If the stem said "the client signs requests with identity pool credentials" instead: AWS_IAM authorization, because the users [obtain temporary credentials](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-aws-iam-with-identity-pool) from an identity pool.
say: Put a Cognito user pool authorizer on the API methods; API Gateway checks the token.

stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and has 12 AWS accounts. Employees sign in to business applications through the company's external SAML 2.0 identity provider. The company also runs a mobile app for its customers. The app's customers must sign in with Google and upload photos to Amazon S3 with short-term credentials. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: The app's customers must sign in with Google
upload photos to Amazon S3 with short-term credentials

options.text: Use IAM Identity Center with the external identity provider as the identity source, and assign permission sets that give access to the AWS accounts.
options.why: IAM Identity Center serves the workforce, and Amazon Cognito is the service to [manage identities for your customer facing applications](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-cognito-is-not-an-identity-source).

options.text: Use an Amazon Cognito user pool that federates with the identity providers that the users already have, and an identity pool that issues temporary AWS credentials.
options.why: The user pool signs customers in with Google, and the identity pool turns the token into [temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool) for the upload.

options.text: Create an IAM user with MFA and an access key for each person in each AWS account, and rotate every access key on a fixed monthly schedule.
options.why: [IAM users are granted long-term credentials](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials), and the stem asks for short-term credentials for every customer.

options.text: Create an IAM identity provider and IAM roles in every AWS account, and build a custom broker that exchanges each sign-in for temporary role credentials.
options.why: It works, but the IAM guide says [whenever possible, use Amazon Cognito](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-preferred-over-direct-web-identity-federation), and the broker is code to build and run.

explanation: The users are customers of the app, not employees. A user pool gives sign-in with customer identities from [Amazon, Google, Apple and Facebook](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-user-pool-workforce-sso-in-your-app), and an identity pool exchanges the token for AWS credentials. The app then uploads to Amazon S3 with credentials that expire, and no key is stored.
takeaway: Customers of an app sign in through a Cognito user pool and reach AWS through an identity pool.
twin: If the stem said "The engineers must sign in once and use the AWS CLI with short-term credentials in every account" instead: IAM Identity Center, because [you only federate once](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-one-point-of-federation).
say: App customers sign in to a user pool, and an identity pool gives the AWS credentials.

stem: A company has one AWS account and does not use AWS Organizations. The company runs AWS Managed Microsoft AD in a VPC for its Windows workloads, and its ten administrators have user accounts in this directory. The administrators must use the AWS Management Console with their directory credentials. The company wants to avoid IAM users. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: one AWS account and does not use AWS Organizations

options.text: Create an IAM user for each administrator with the same name and password as in the directory, and require MFA for each IAM user.
options.why: The company wants to avoid IAM users, and [IAM users are granted long-term credentials](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials) that are separate from the directory passwords.

options.text: Enable an account instance of IAM Identity Center in the account, connect the directory, and assign permission sets to the administrators' group.
options.why: Permission sets are [available only for organization instances](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-permission-sets-need-organization-instance), so an account instance has none to assign.

options.text: Create an access URL for the directory, assign an IAM role to the directory group of the administrators, and let them sign in at that URL.
options.why: Directory Service lets you [assign IAM roles](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-console-sso-iam-roles) to directory groups, and the administrators sign in at [a customer-specific URL](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-console-sso-iam-roles) with their directory credentials.

options.text: Create an organization in AWS Organizations, enable an organization instance of IAM Identity Center, connect the directory as its identity source, and assign permission sets to the administrators.
options.why: It works, but it adds an organization and an IAM Identity Center instance for one account, which IAM roles for the directory serve with less work.
options.misconception: creates an organization and a sign-in service to give console access in a single account

explanation: Directory members [do not have access to any AWS resources](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-console-access-iam-roles-access-url) until you give it. [You assign IAM roles to your directory members](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-console-access-iam-roles-access-url), and [your directory must have an access URL](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-console-access-iam-roles-access-url). The administrators then sign in with their directory credentials, and no IAM user exists.
takeaway: Directory users of one account reach the console through IAM roles and the access URL of the directory.
twin: If the stem said "40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations" instead: IAM Identity Center with the directory as identity source, because it gives [single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-wa-two-federation-approaches).
say: In one account, assign IAM roles to the directory groups and use the directory's access URL.

stem: A company has an Active Directory domain in its on-premises data center and a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the data center and a VPC. The company is moving several workloads to AWS. The domain controllers can be reached from the VPC. Amazon RDS for SQL Server databases must use Windows Authentication with the employees' existing AD accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create a Simple AD directory in the VPC, and create a two-way trust between the Simple AD directory and the on-premises domain.
options.why: Simple AD [does not support multi-factor authentication (MFA), trust relationships](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-simple-ad-unsupported-features), and it is [not compatible with RDS SQL Server](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-simple-ad-unsupported-features).

options.text: Create an AD Connector in the VPC that points to the on-premises domain controllers, and register the directory with the AWS services that need it.
options.why: Amazon RDS [is not compatible with AD Connector](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-rds-needs-managed-ad), so the databases cannot use this directory for Windows Authentication.

options.text: Launch Amazon EC2 instances in the VPC as additional domain controllers of the on-premises domain, and let Active Directory replicate the whole domain to the instances.
options.why: Domain controllers on EC2 are instances that the company patches and backs up itself; AWS Managed Microsoft AD includes [host monitoring, recovery, data replication, snapshots](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-managed-ad-dc-pair-across-azs).
options.misconception: runs its own domain controllers on instances instead of a managed directory

options.text: Create an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory in the VPC, and create a two-way forest trust between that directory and the on-premises domain.
options.why: RDS is [compatible with AWS Managed Microsoft AD only](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-rds-needs-managed-ad), and RDS works with [either a one-way or two-way trust](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-two-way-trust-for-aws-apps-one-way-for-ec2-rds-fsx) to the on-premises domain.

explanation: Windows Authentication for RDS needs a directory that RDS supports, and RDS is [compatible with AWS Managed Microsoft AD only](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-rds-needs-managed-ad). A forest trust lets the employees' existing accounts sign in, because AWS Managed Microsoft AD supports [one and two-way external and forest trust relationships](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-trust-types-and-directions). AWS runs the domain controllers.
takeaway: Amazon RDS for SQL Server with Windows Authentication needs AWS Managed Microsoft AD, with a trust for on-premises accounts.
twin: If the stem said "Employees must sign in to Amazon WorkSpaces with their existing AD credentials, and user accounts must remain only in the on-premises directory" instead: AD Connector, because it [forwards sign-in requests to your on-premises Active Directory](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-ad-connector-is-a-proxy).
say: RDS for SQL Server needs AWS Managed Microsoft AD, with a trust to the on-premises domain.

stem: A company runs a hybrid environment. Its on-premises data center has two Active Directory forests, and AWS Direct Connect links the data center to a VPC in the AWS Organizations management account. The company uses IAM Identity Center for access to many AWS accounts. Employees from both forests must sign in to IAM Identity Center with their existing Active Directory credentials. What is the MOST operationally efficient way to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create AWS Managed Microsoft AD in the management account, create a two-way forest trust to each forest, and set the directory as the identity source.
options.why: With AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the source, IAM Identity Center works with users from [any domain connected through an AD trust](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-ad-via-trust-to-self-managed), and two-way trusts meet its requirement.

options.text: Create one AD Connector for each forest in the management account, and connect both AD Connector directories to IAM Identity Center as identity sources.
options.why: IAM Identity Center can [connect only one AD Connector directory](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-one-ad-directory-managed-ad-for-multiple-forests) at a time, so two forests need another design.

options.text: Create AWS Managed Microsoft AD in the management account, create a one-way forest trust to each forest, and set the directory as the identity source.
options.why: IAM Identity Center [requires a two-way trust](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-needs-two-way-trust-not-one-way), and [one-way trusts do not work](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-needs-two-way-trust-not-one-way) with it.

options.text: Migrate the users of both forests into AWS Managed Microsoft AD with the Active Directory Migration Toolkit (ADMT), and set the directory as the identity source.
options.why: It works, but AWS [does not provide any migration tools](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-managed-ad-no-migration-tools-standard-enterprise), so the company plans the whole move, which is more work than two trusts.
options.misconception: moves every user into AWS before IAM Identity Center can use the users

explanation: AWS says to use AWS Managed Microsoft AD to [support multiple domains or forests](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-one-ad-directory-managed-ad-for-multiple-forests). IAM Identity Center [requires a two-way trust](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-needs-two-way-trust-not-one-way) to each forest. With this source, [no password information is synchronized](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-ad-pass-through-no-passwords-synced), so the passwords stay in the forests.
takeaway: Several on-premises forests reach IAM Identity Center through AWS Managed Microsoft AD with two-way trusts.
twin: If the stem said "one Active Directory forest with one domain" instead: AD Connector, because it [forwards sign-in requests to your on-premises Active Directory](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-ad-connector-is-a-proxy) without a directory in AWS.
say: Two forests means AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a two-way trust to each forest.

stem: A company hosts an internet-facing web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The load balancer has an HTTPS listener with a certificate. The company sells the application to business customers. Each customer's employees must sign in with that customer's corporate SAML 2.0 identity provider before any request reaches the instances. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
keywords: before any request reaches the instances

options.text: Add each customer's SAML identity provider to IAM Identity Center as an identity source, and assign the web application to each customer's employees.
options.why: IAM Identity Center connects [only one directory or one SAML 2.0 identity provider](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-one-identity-source-at-a-time) at a time, and it serves the company's own workforce.

options.text: Create a Cognito user pool with each customer's SAML identity provider, and add an authenticate-cognito action to a new HTTP listener on port 80.
options.why: The authenticate-cognito action is [supported only with HTTPS listeners](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-alb-authenticate-cognito-https-only), so a rule on an HTTP listener does not sign users in.

options.text: Create a Cognito user pool with each customer's SAML identity provider, and add an authenticate-cognito action to the rules of the existing HTTPS listener.
options.why: The load balancer can [offload the work of authenticating users](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-alb-authenticate-cognito-https-only) to the user pool, so a request reaches the instances after the user signs in.

options.text: Put an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API in front of the load balancer, and write a Lambda authorizer that validates the SAML assertions of each customer.
options.why: It works, but the team writes and runs SAML code that the user pool and the load balancer provide without code.
options.misconception: believes that sign-in with a corporate SAML provider needs custom authorizer code

explanation: The load balancer signs users in before it forwards a request, and the action is [supported only with HTTPS listeners](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-alb-authenticate-cognito-https-only), which the stem has. The user pool accepts each customer's SAML provider and [issues JSON web tokens (JWTs)](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-saml-idp-must-support-saml-2) of its own, so the application needs no sign-in code.
takeaway: An Application Load Balancer can sign users in through a Cognito user pool, on an HTTPS listener.
twin: If the stem said "customers sign in with Google" instead: the same listener rule works, because a user pool also federates [Amazon, Google, Apple and Facebook](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-user-pool-workforce-sso-in-your-app).
say: Let the load balancer sign users in through a Cognito user pool on the HTTPS listener.

steps: I read the last sentence first: it asks for the solution with the LEAST development effort.

I mark the constraints: an internet-facing Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener, the corporate SAML 2.0 identity provider of each customer, and sign-in before any request reaches the instances.

Before I look at the options, I predict a Cognito user pool with the SAML providers and an authenticate-cognito rule on the load balancer, because the load balancer can sign users in before it forwards a request.

I remove IAM Identity Center, because it connects one SAML identity provider at a time and serves the company's own workforce. I remove API Gateway with a Lambda authorizer, because SAML checks in a function are code to write and run.

Between the two user pool options the difference is the listener; the stem says the load balancer has an HTTPS listener, and the authenticate-cognito action works on HTTPS listeners only, so I keep the rule on the existing HTTPS listener.
Check: the user pool with the rule on the HTTPS listener meets every constraint and needs no sign-in code. Time: 90 seconds.

stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and manages workforce access with IAM Identity Center. An administrator creates a permission set that holds an AWS managed policy for read-only access. The administrator assigns the permission set to the group of auditors for one member account. Later, a security engineer reviews the IAM resources of that member account. What does the engineer find that IAM Identity Center created for this assignment?
keywords: assigns the permission set to the group of auditors
IAM resources of that member account

options.text: One IAM user for each auditor, with a console password and the read-only policy
options.why: IAM Identity Center [does not create IAM users and groups](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users); the auditors stay in its own identity store.

options.text: One IAM group for the auditors, with the read-only policy attached to the IAM group
options.why: The auditors group stays in IAM Identity Center, because it [does not create IAM users and groups](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users) in the accounts.

options.text: A resource-based policy on each resource in the account that names the auditors group
options.why: A permission set holds identity-based policies, and IAM Identity Center [attaches the policies specified in the permission set](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-permission-set-change-updates-roles) to a role.
options.misconception: believes that a permission set is applied as resource-based policies on each resource

options.text: One IAM role whose name begins with AWSReservedSSO_ and that has the read-only policy
options.why: IAM Identity Center [creates and manages IAM roles](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users), and the AWSReservedSSO_ prefix shows that the role [came from assigning a permission set](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-roles-named-awsreservedsso).

explanation: A permission set is [a template that you create and maintain](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-permission-set-is-policy-template). When it is assigned to an account, IAM Identity Center creates a role for it there and [attaches the policies specified in the permission set](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-permission-set-change-updates-roles). The auditors sign in to IAM Identity Center and get a session of that role.
takeaway: A permission set becomes an IAM role in each assigned account, and IAM Identity Center [does not create IAM users and groups](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users).
twin: If the stem said "the administrator later adds a policy to the permission set" instead: the same role changes, because the [corresponding IAM policies and roles are updated accordingly](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-permission-set-change-updates-roles).
say: A permission set becomes one role in each assigned account, named AWSReservedSSO.

stem: A company builds a mobile quiz app. People can play before they create an account, and the app writes each quiz result to an Amazon DynamoDB table directly from the device. The writes must use temporary AWS credentials. Players who have not signed in must also be able to save their results, and the company will add sign-in later. Which Amazon Cognito feature gives the players who have not signed in these credentials?
keywords: players who have not signed in

options.text: A user pool app client that is created without a client secret
options.why: An app client lets the app call the user pool, and the user pool is there to [issue JSON web tokens (JWTs)](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool), not AWS credentials.

options.text: An identity pool that allows guest access and has an unauthenticated IAM role
options.why: An identity pool can [issue limited-privilege credentials to guest users](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-identity-pool-guest-credentials), and [a separate IAM role](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-identity-pool-unauthenticated-guest-role) sets what guests can do.

options.text: A user pool group that has an IAM role attached to the user pool group
options.why: A user pool can give a [role to a group](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-group-precedence-preferred-role), but that role reaches the app through the ID token of a signed-in user.
options.misconception: believes that a user pool group role works for players who have not signed in

options.text: An IAM Identity Center permission set that is assigned to each player
options.why: IAM Identity Center serves the workforce, and Amazon Cognito is the service to [manage identities for your customer facing applications](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-cognito-is-not-an-identity-source).

explanation: Guests have no token, so a user pool has nothing to give them. An identity pool can [issue limited-privilege credentials to guest users](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-identity-pool-guest-credentials), and guests [access your app as a guest](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-identity-pool-unauthenticated-guest-role) with their own role. That role [should be more restrictive](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-unauthenticated-role-more-restrictive) than the role for signed-in users.
takeaway: Guests of an app get temporary AWS credentials from an identity pool with an unauthenticated role.
twin: If the stem said "players sign in with Google before they play" instead: the identity pool uses its authenticated role, because it accepts [a SAML assertion, or a social-provider OAuth token](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-identity-pool-directory-of-federated-identities).
say: Guests get credentials from an identity pool with an unauthenticated role.
